n: William E. McLellin, a schoolteacher baptized that summer, had secretly prayed for answers to five questions. The Lord blesses him for turning from sin and accepting the truth. McLellin later testified this revelation answered all his questions.

f.g: Later one of the original Twelve Apostles (1835); he left the Church in 1838.

n: He is blessed for receiving the everlasting covenant—the fulness of the gospel—which brings life and glories foretold by ancient prophets and apostles.
He is clean, but not entirely; he must repent of what displeases the Lord, who will show him what it is.

f.w: you are clean, but not all

n: The Lord will reveal his will for William.
He is to preach the gospel from land to land and city to city, especially where it hasn’t been preached.
Don’t stay long here or go to Zion yet. Send what you can there, but don’t worry about property.
Go to the eastern states, testify everywhere, reasoning with people in their places of worship.
Samuel H. Smith should go with him; William must not abandon him, but should teach him. The faithful will be strengthened, and the Lord will go with them.
Bless the sick, and they will recover. Don’t return until sent. Be patient in trials. Ask and knock.

f.w: Lay your hands upon the sick, and they shall recover

n: Avoid being weighed down by distractions; forsake unrighteousness; don’t commit adultery—a temptation William had struggled with. The Lord knows each person’s specific weaknesses.

f.g: Burdened or weighed down with cares.

n: Keep these words; magnify your calling; and you will push many people to Zion singing songs of everlasting joy.

f.g: Fulfill one’s calling fully and honorably.

n: Continue faithfully to the end and receive a crown of eternal life at the Father’s right hand.
The revelation is signed by Jesus Christ, the Redeemer.
